title: J012--Fire Suppression System Maintenance and
description: Site Visit: A site visit will be held on December 1, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. ET. Interested vendors should meet at building 6 at the Richard L. Roudebush VA Medical Center, 1481 W. 10th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46202. See map and pinned location below for building 6. Following the walkthrough of the main hospital, vendors may attend an additional walkthrough at the off-site location: 9045 East 59th Street, Building 402, Indianapolis, IN 46216. Please note that transportation to the off-site location will not be provided by the VA. RFI Responses Submitted by: Gunnar Sager, COO, FinalLine Solutions L.L.C. INFORMATION NEEDED: 1.Site visit PWS §§ 7, 8, 11 and Appendix A. Can the VA arrange a pre-quote site visit at both the main medical center and Building 402 for FinalLine Solutions and its prospective kitchen exhaust cleaning and fire protection subcontractors? We would like to see the three Canteen hoods (C-1166), the Production Kitchen hood (C-B144) and its upper-floor duct and fan connections, the rooftop exhaust fans, the Building 402 hood, suppression system and grease trap, and the Kidde IND-21 units at Buildings 1 and 22. Please provide available dates and times, the meeting location, and any registration, escort or ID requirements. Yes, a pre-quote site visit can be arranged. 2.Exhaust duct routes and access PWS § 7 and Appendix A.2. PWS § 7 refers to "the eight previously listed main-campus duct systems." Please identify those eight systems. Can the VA also provide any available duct drawings or route sketches, fan and access-panel locations, and known inaccessible sections, particularly for the Production Kitchen and the fourth- and fifth-floor connections? If a site visit cannot be arranged, please provide any photos or prior cleaning reports that show existing access conditions. The eight systems were a reference to language in the previous contract. The PWS has been updated to remove that language, as the VA is uncertain what it was referring to. The PWS has also been updated to include exhaust fan locations. The rest can be determined by a site visit. Previous cleaning reports, including one dated April 2026 is attached, that includes photos in response to this RFI. 3.Building 402 grease trap PWS §§ 8, 11 and Appendix A.3. Please confirm the trap type and capacity (gallons), the cover location, and the approved overnight pump-truck staging location. If known, please provide the approximate hose distance from the staging point to the trap and any vehicle size, weight or access restrictions. Unknown. Can be determined by the offeror during scheduled site visit. 4.Building 402 equipment Appendix A.1 and A.2. Please confirm the make, model and agent type of the Building 402 kitchen suppression system (KS-05) and the exhaust fan ID serving hood KH-05. Unknown. Can be determined by the offeror during a scheduled site visit. 5.Prior service history PWS § 5 and Appendix A.4. PWS § 5 requires the schedule to use verified prior service dates and states that a contract transition does not restart intervals. Please provide the current or most recent contractor's service records, or at minimum the last completion dates, for each suppression unit (monthly, semiannual and annual), each hood cleaning (KH-01 to KH-05) and the GT-01 pump-out. Please also identify any work currently overdue. According to our records it is believed to be as follows: KH-1 to KH-04 Fire Semi-Annual Inspections were completed on 10/20/2026. Cleanings for these systems were completed on 10/26/2026. KH-5 was cleaned in September 2026, the Semi-annual inspection date is unknown and assumed due. GT-01 was cleaned in September 2026. HM-01 to HM-05 Semi-annual inspections were completed on 10/20/2026. 6.Extended-interval testing PWS § 9 and Appendix A.4. Please identify any extended-interval maintenance or testing known to be due during the base or option years, along with the affected system IDs and anticipated due dates. If any of this work must be priced with the quote, please identify the applicable line item. See updated pricing schedule attached. 7.Personnel credentialing VAAR 852.204-70 and 852.204-72; PWS § 11. Will contractor and subcontractor technicians performing recurring monthly and quarterly service need PIV cards or background investigations, or will VA-issued temporary or visitor badges be sufficient? Please identify any processing lead time needed before the first visit. Contractor and subcontractor personnel must satisfy the applicable VA personnel-vetting and credentialing requirements before beginning work. The required investigation level, identification credential, and processing lead time will be confirmed by the CO in coordination with the responsible VA security personnel. A visitor badge shall not be assumed to replace required vetting. 8.Price schedule format Solicitation § B.2; PWS § 2 and Appendix B. Section B.2 requests a single monthly price for each performance year, while PWS § 2 calls for separately identifiable service categories. Will the VA accept the completed B.2 schedule with a separate supporting price breakdown by service category (monthly suppression inspections, semiannual suppression service, hood inspection and cleaning, grease trap service), or is there a required format? title: Borough of Millvale, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: The Millvale LPP was constructed by U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) in 1980 under the authority of Section 205 of the Flood Control Act of 1948 as amended. The project consists of about 6,200 feet of channel improvement including concrete gravity retaining walls, concrete wall supports, anchored concrete toe blocks, concrete cap walls, stone-filled gabion mattresses, flap gates and access ramps. The LPP is an urban Flood Control Work (FCW), and it is not a multipurpose project. Heavy rains from 1-12 April 2024 caused flooding which damaged the Project within Girtys Run, including bank erosion, shoaling, erosion of the improved channel, ruptured gabion baskets, washed-out concrete buttresses, and erosion of grouted riprap. Of particular concern are the washed-out buttresses which have migrated to the center of the improved channel, impeding streamflow. If the buttresses are not removed and stream bank improvements continue to deteriorate, there is a risk that debris will continue to accumulate and could ultimately damage the channel downstream of the impediment. To address these damages, Allegheny County requested rehabilitation assistance from USACE through the PL 84-99 program, which authorizes USACE to rehabilitate eligible Federal and non-Federal LPPs damaged or destroyed by floods. An agreement was signed on 6 August 2025 between the Borough of Millvale and USACE to complete the necessary repairs. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $300,000.00 and $350,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The anticipated award date is 22 December 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO Part 13 and 36, price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that exceed available funds for this requirement. Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/ then scrolling down on right hand side of page by clicking on View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here.

title: OCAS_RFI_360Camera
description: The General Services Administration (GSA) is conducting market research to identify commercially available, handheld 360-degree cameras capable of capturing visual construction-progress documentation for federal facilities. Captured media will be handled as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and ingested into a FedRAMP-authorized IT system via removable media or a direct encrypted connection to that system. The Government seeks a capture device that operates independently of vendor cloud services and consumer mobile applications. The Government will consider two capture configurations, described in Section 2.3. The offline configuration transfers imagery by removable media. title: France – Research and experimental development services – Développement d’une méthode de projection d’argile destinée au remplissage des zones de dépose de revêtement dans les ouvrages de scellement de Cigéo
description: Le marché porte sur l’étude, le développement et la validation d’une solution innovante de projection d’argile destinée au remplissage des zones de dépose des ouvrages de scellement des galeries horizontales de Cigéo (Centre industriel de stockage géologique des déchets radioactifs français). Il vise à définir une formulation du matériau ainsi qu’un procédé de projection garantissant la stabilité et la tenue du remplissage au contact de la roche hôte du Callovo-Oxfordien (Cox). L’optimisation de cette solution sera conduite au travers d’essais réalisés à différentes échelles, depuis le laboratoire de surface jusqu’au laboratoire souterrain du Centre de Meuse et Haute Marne de l'Andra.

title: Demolition of an existing building, Site Improvements and construction of a Modular Office Building at the US Merchant Marine Academy Campus, Kings Point, NY
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District is issuing an invitation for bid to award a Firm Fixed Price construction contract for the demolition of existing building, site Improvements and provide a turnkey modular office facility. The scope includes the demolition of an existing 10,000 SF building (with basement, in-ground pool, and pool shed), Hazardous Materials Abatement and Disposal, Site Improvements (SWPPP Controls, Sidewalks, Parking, Landscaping, Temp Fencing, Utilities Infrastructure including Water, Sewer, Electrical, Telecom tie-ins), and construction of a new office space of approximately 5,700 square feet, composed of custom modular units. The facility will be a single-story complex with a u-shaped space opening onto a small deck. It will house open offices with cubicles, six private offices, two conference rooms, four single-user bathrooms, a kitchenette/pantry room, lactation room, storage closets, and a mechanical room. The project scope encompasses incidental demolition, site prep work, foundations, underground utility hook ups, and site lighting. The contractor will also be responsible for providing furniture, fixtures, and equipment based upon the drawings and specifications. The building and site infrastructure are required to have a minimum life expectancy of 10 to 15 years. The contract duration will be 136 calendar days for the entire project with phasing work involved. NAICS: 236220 Size standard: $45 million. Project magnitude is between $1,000,000 - $5,000,000.

description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction, Project NP NER PMS BMS FY25(2), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000004, located in Essex County, New Jersey; Pike, Wayne, and Lackawanna Counties, Pennsylvania; and the City of Baltimore, Maryland. The project consists of roadway and bridge maintenance at Thomas Edison National Historical Park (EDIS), Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine (FOMC), Steamtown National Historic Site (STEA), and Upper Delaware Scenic and Recreational River (UPDE). buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Baxter/Hill-Rom Helux Pro Surgical Light System
description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA), Intramural Research Program (IRP), operates the Clinical Research Unit (CRU) located at the MedStar Harbor Hospital campus in Baltimore, Maryland. The CRU serves as the primary dedicated clinical facility supporting human longitudinal and translational aging research protocols, including the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA), the Genetic and Epigenetic Signatures of Translational Aging Laboratory Testing (GESTALT) study, and specialized clinical trials investigating age-related functional decline and metabolic disorders. A cornerstone of these intramural clinical protocols involves invasive outpatient biopsy procedures�specifically percutaneous skeletal muscle biopsies, subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsies, and dermal skin punch biopsies. These procedures provide vital biospecimens for cellular, molecular, and physiological characterization of human aging. The existing ceiling-mounted surgical lighting system currently deployed in the CRU procedure suite has reached the end of its useful service life (End-of-Life / EOL). The legacy unit is experiencing persistent operational failures. Critical replacement parts are no longer manufactured or supported by the original equipment manufacturer (OEM), rendering the existing unit non-serviceable. Because medical-grade illumination is a non-negotiable safety and operational prerequisite for procedural asepsis, precise anatomical depth perception, tissue differentiation, and hemostasis, the current state presents an unacceptable clinical risk and threatens immediate disruption to approved NIA protocol timelines.

title: Demolition of an existing building, Site Improvements and construction of a Modular Office Building at the US Merchant Marine Academy Campus, Kings Point, NY
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District is issuing an invitation for bid to award a Firm Fixed Price construction contract for the demolition of existing building, site Improvements and provide a turnkey modular office facility. The scope includes the demolition of an existing 10,000 SF building (with basement, in-ground pool, and pool shed), Hazardous Materials Abatement and Disposal, Site Improvements (SWPPP Controls, Sidewalks, Parking, Landscaping, Temp Fencing, Utilities Infrastructure including Water, Sewer, Electrical, Telecom tie-ins), and construction of a new office space of approximately 5,700 square feet, composed of custom modular units. The facility will be a single-story complex with a u-shaped space opening onto a small deck. It will house open offices with cubicles, six private offices, two conference rooms, four single-user bathrooms, a kitchenette/pantry room, lactation room, storage closets, and a mechanical room. The project scope encompasses incidental demolition, site prep work, foundations, underground utility hook ups, and site lighting. The contractor will also be responsible for providing furniture, fixtures, and equipment based upon the drawings and specifications. The building and site infrastructure are required to have a minimum life expectancy of 10 to 15 years. The contract duration will be 136 calendar days for the entire project with phasing work involved. NAICS: 236220 Size standard: $45 million. Project magnitude is between $1,000,000 - $5,000,000.

title: Repair Aids to Navigation (ATON) - Southern Area of USCG District Northeast
description: Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision and disposal required for the structural repair, recapitalization, and/or demolish Aids to Navigation (ATON) structures at various southern sites in the CG Northeast District. The project consists of a Base Bid at the following sites in New York, Connecticut and Rhode Island: 1. New Haven Middle Breakwater West End Light (LLNR 24070): Replace existing tower in kind. 2. Stonington Outer Breakwater Light 4 (LLNR 20170): Replace existing concrete foundation, replace existing tower with standard 5x5 tower. 3. Stonington Breakwater Light 5 (LLNR 20175): Replace existing concrete foundation, repoint existing granite block foundation, replace existing tower in kind. 4. Norwalk Channel Light 10 (LLNR 24990): Replace existing foundation and tower in kind. 5. Port Jefferson West Breakwater Light 2A (LLNR 26145): Replace existing foundation and tower in kind. 6. Connecticut River Light 135 (LLNR 23300): Demolish ATON structure to below-grade elevation & reseed. 7. Point Judith Harbor of Refuge West Entrance Light 3 (LLNR 19505):Demolish existing structure & rebuild as standard 5x5 tower on concrete foundation offset from jetty erosion. An option item for an additional Aid to Navigation (ATON) structure repair in Massachusetts is included as follows: 1. Chatham Light (LLNR 525): Replace windows in kind & clean/recoat exterior/interior. The estimated value of the procurement is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. A 20% bid guarantee is required. Performance and Payment bonds will be required. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. Solicitation packages will be available on or about 4 November 2026. The tentative date set for receipt of bids is 8 December 2026 at 2:00 p.m. The base performance period is estimated to be 300 calendar days from issuance of Notice to Proceed and the option performance period is estimated to be 60 calendar days to be exercised at the Contracting Officers discretion. This acquisition is issued pursuant to FAR Part 14 Sealed Bidding and is 100% Set-Aside for Small Business concerns. All relevant solicitation documents, including specifications and drawings may be accessed for download beginning on the date of issue of the IFB at the following site: https://www.sam.gov. Vendors MUST be registered in the System for Award Management database through https://www.sam.gov in order to receive a federal government contract. THE GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THIS SOLICITATION EITHER BEFORE OR AFTER THE CLOSING DATE. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS PRESOLICITATION NOTICE OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUEST.

title: Maintenance Support Building (MSB) Parking Lot Renovation
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR MARKET RESEARCH ONLY � This Notice does not constitute a solicitation announcement or restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach and NO AWARD will occur from this Notice. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT Notice to determine the capabilities of both small AND large business firms. Qualified companies, regardless of their size or socio-economic status, are encouraged to respond. Two or more small business firms capable of performing this work may help to guide the acquisition strategy and influence potential set-aside. Businesses are strongly encouraged to review this SOURCES SOUGHT and submit according to the directions in this notice. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement for this requirement. Based on the responses to this sources sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses (in full or in part) or procured through full and open competition. All small business set-aside categories will be considered. Both Large and Small Business firms who are interested are encouraged to respond to this Sources Sought Notice. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted nor acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding submissions. This is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Invitation for Bid (IFB) and is for market research purposes only. Project Description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking qualified Contractors to rehabilitate and modernize the historic Maintenance Support Building (MSB) west parking lot at the Soo Locks facility in Sault Ste. Marie, Chippewa County, MI. With an estimated construction range between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000, this project includes concrete paving, utility demolition, stormwater management, and physical security upgrades. The site carries a historic designation, so the design includes specialized fencing and lighting as well as relocation of two large concrete pylons at the entry drive. The scope requires the complete demolition of the existing concrete lot, removal of designated trees, and installation of new reinforced concrete pavement. Paving design and materials will generally follow Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT) standards. Fencelines will be relocated to accommodate overflow parking and snow storage using fabricated ornamental black fencing. The existing stormwater collection system will be removed and replaced in its entirety. The Contractor will demolish an existing transformer and associated feeds, and connect new parking lot lighting, gate operators, and security systems to stubs from an electrical panel. Security improvements include providing a reconfigured sallyport-style vehicle entry using two motorized vehicle gates. A new steel-cable vehicle crash restraint system will be installed on the front fenceline, along with security cameras and a secure pedestrian entrance. The scope will include a new foundation and infrastructure for which to place a government-furnished guard shack. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS are available for this Notice. NAICS Code: 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction with a size standard of $45,500,000.00. Instructions: Please complete the attached Sources Sought Survey and return it via email to the points of contact listed below. Failure to provide a complete response may result in the Government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. Any information submitted by Respondents to this Sources Sought synopsis is voluntary. As stipulated in Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 15.101, responses to this Notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Any information submitted by Respondents to this Sources Sought synopsis is voluntary and will not be returned. The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred or associated with the submission of information in response to this Notice. The decision to solicit for a contract shall be solely within the Government's discretion. Additional company capability information is welcome. Your company�s response is limited to 5 pages. All attachments must be provided in either Microsoft Word, Excel, or Adobe Acrobat PDF format. Attachments with files ending in �.zip� or �.exe� are not allowable and files will be stripped and deleted from any emails received by the Government. Ensure only .pdf, .docx, or .xls(x) documents are attached to your email. Please send responses no later than 2:00 PM EST on December 8th, 2026. PLEASE REFERENCE �SOURCES SOUGHT: MSB Parking Lot Renovation�, in the subject line. Please respond to Sources Sought Survey in the attachment and email it to LRE-Proposal@usace.army.mil, sally.e.artz@usace.army.mil, and michelle.barr@usace.army.mil. If you have any questions or concerns, please contact us via the aforementioned email addresses. Your prompt attention and response to this Notice is greatly appreciated. All data received in response to this Sources Sought that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government.

description: Description THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY � Solicitations are not available at this time. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government and respondents will not be entitled to payment of direct or indirect cost incurred in responding to this request for information (RFI). The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Acquisition and Grants Office (AGO), Corporate Services Acquisition Division (CSAD), located in Silver Spring, MD, is conducting market research to identify businesses and organizations capable of providing specialized space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. The Government is also seeking information on industry capabilities and approaches for providing flexible, on-demand access to qualified subject matter experts, including short-notice consultations, rapid-turn analyses, and longer-duration support. Responses will help assess the availability of qualified sources, industry capacity to meet varying response timelines, and potential acquisition approaches, including consideration of a multiple-award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). NAICS CODE: To be determined Background The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Office of Space Commerce (OSC), is the principal unit for space commerce policy activities within the Department of Commerce. OSC's mission is to foster the conditions for the economic growth and technological advancement of the U.S. commercial space industry. Within OSC, the Policy, Advocacy, and International Division (PAID) supports the development and coordination of domestic and international space commerce policies, promotes U.S. commercial space interests, and engages with government, industry, and international stakeholders on emerging space policy issues. Given the rapidly evolving commercial space environment, PAID requires timely access to specialized expertise, research, data, and analysis to support policy development, strategic planning, and leadership decision-making. These needs may arise with little advance notice and range from brief consultations with subject matter experts to comprehensive research, policy assessments, and longer-duration advisory support. PAID is exploring approaches to obtaining these services that provide flexibility, timely access to qualified experts, and cost-effective support across a broad range of space policy matters. Purpose The purpose of this RFI is to better understand industry capabilities, service delivery approaches, and associated costs and benefits for providing flexible, on-demand space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. Specifically, the Government seeks information on vendors' demonstrated expertise across the identified Task Areas, their ability to provide timely access to qualified subject matter experts, and their capacity to support both short-duration consultations and more extensive analytical requirements. The Government is also interested in understanding whether these capabilities are available through vendors' existing personnel, established subcontractor or consultant relationships, or other arrangements. Responses will assist OSC in refining its requirements, evaluating potential acquisition and ordering approaches, and determining how best to obtain timely, cost-effective access to specialized expertise. Although this RFI requests specific information, it is not intended to discourage creative thinking on the part of the industry to propose alternative solutions or approaches that the Government may not have considered. Scope and Draft Requirements The attached draft PWS describes seven potential task areas. Respondents may identify one or more areas of demonstrated capability: Commercial Space Policy and Regulation � U.S. commercial space policy, licensing, permitting, regulatory oversight, and interagency issues. Space Traffic Coordination, Safety, and Sustainability � Civil space traffic coordination, SSA, conjunction coordination, debris mitigation, standards and norms. International and Geopolitical Space Policy � International governance, UNCOPUOS, foreign regulatory regimes, geopolitical implications. Space Law and Regulatory Analysis � Domestic/international legal and regulatory research and analysis; not legal representation. Commercial Space Industry and Economic Policy � Commercial space markets, competitiveness, investment, industry data, indicators and economic impacts. Emerging Space Activities and Technology Policy � Policy implications of RPO, in-space servicing, commercial stations, lunar activities, remote sensing and novel services. Strategic and Executive Advisory Support � Expert consultations, executive briefings, workshops, time-sensitive research and decision-support analysis. Potential forms of support include: Consultation Only; Consultation Plus Summary; Research and Analytical Services; Data and Information Services; and Extended Support. Services may be ordered individually or together. The draft PWS describes Rapid (several hours to one business day), Expedited (generally one to two business days), and Standard quotation/availability response categories. These are response expectations, not automatic performance-completion deadlines. The contemplated BPA would have a five-year ordering period, with requirements, schedules, deliverables and pricing established at the individual Call level. The Government has not determined the final acquisition vehicle, number of awards, or ordering procedures. Responses Responses to this RFI must be submitted using the Market Research Questionnaire located at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdnCIev0vZbNRslzShVW9nCFj-Pe_UgXVdsSmlADasb05Fztg/viewform by Friday, December 8, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

title: 2027 NIAID DMID Omnibus Broad Agency Announcement: Development of Medical Interventions for Infectious Diseases
description: INTRODUCTION: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), one of 27 institutes of the NIH, an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS); conducts and supports research to understand, treat, and ultimately prevent the myriad infectious, immunologic, and allergic diseases that threaten the health and longevity of human lives.Through a variety of research grants and contracts, NIAID�s Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) specifically supports extramural research to develop new medical interventions against infectious disease threats to include drug-resistant pathogens. NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to help address goals articulated in a number of strategic plans, such as in the Public Health Emergency Medical Countermeasures Enterprise Strategy and Implementation Plan (https://aspr.hhs.gov/PHEMCE/2024-PHEMCE-SIP/Pages/default.aspx), as well as current prioritized antimicrobial resistant threats identified by national death and infection estimates as determined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention�s (CDC) to prevent and control antimicrobial resistance (https://www.cdc.gov/antimicrobial-resistance/data-research/threats/index.html). In addition, NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to encourage projects that align with the NIH priorities of enhancing rigor & reproducibility, improving biosafety and biosecurity, and the use of complementary non-animal testing methods where appropriate. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is soliciting proposals to advance the research and development of promising candidate therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics for infectious diseases in each of three (3) Research Areas described below and more thoroughly discussed in the attached BAA Solicitation. An offeror should carefully review the content of the BAA Solicitation No. HHS-NIH-NIAID-BAA2026-1 for the comprehensive information regarding all requirements, the technical objective of each Research Area of this BAA Solicitation, instructions regarding the proposal submission, and a description of the evaluation and award process. Please note, due to the competitive nature of the BAA Solicitation, the NIAID is unable to offer advice or feedback regarding an offeror�s specific technical approach. Offerors should exercise their professional judgment when compiling their proposals in line with the requirements and specifications of the BAA Solicitation. Research Area 001 - Vaccine Candidates: The objective is to develop vaccine candidates through an early phase clinical trial that use a needle free (i.e., alternative to classical needle and syringe, see below for description) route of delivery to protect against infections caused by viral pathogens that include but are not limited to respiratory and vector borne viruses. The scope of this vaccine research area includes the preclinical development of a needle free vaccine candidate, IND enabling studies, limited process development, Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliant manufacturing, regulatory submissions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and conduct of a Phase 1 or early Phase 2 clinical trial. The scope of work must include a clinical trial. Offerors must propose a single vaccine candidate for protection against a specific viral pathogen. The vaccine candidate may provide a breadth of protection against other viral strains or viruses. A strong justification is required to support (1) the proposed vaccine antigen and platform for the disease indication, (2) the use of a clinically relevant adjuvant (if needed), and (3) a clinically relevant needle free route of delivery. Research Area 002 - Therapeutic Candidates: The objective is to develop safe, effective, new therapeutic products that will improve patient outcomes against serious infectious diseases for which there are no approved therapeutics, or for those that are refractory to treatment despite appropriate antimicrobial therapy or due to pathogen resistance. Infectious diseases caused by the following viruses, bacteria and fungi pathogens are targeted: Viral hemorrhagic fever viruses (e.g., EBOV, SUDV, MARV, LASV, hantavirus) https://www.cdc.gov/viral-hemorrhagic-fevers/about/index.html Encephalitic paramyxoviruses (e.g. hendra virus, nipah virus) Picornaviruses (broad spectrum approaches that include EV68, EV70 and coxsackie virus) At least two of the following (i.e., addressed with a broad spectrum antimicrobial): susceptible and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), susceptible and multidrug resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and susceptible and Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter (CRAB), with potential to improve patient outcomes in the clinic; Candida auris, Cryptococcus spp., Aspergillus fumigatus, and/or Mucorales Adjunct medical interventions to support or enhance effectiveness of antimicrobial agents to address underlying pathology that is not resolved after clearance of pathogens, may be considered. Important notice to Offerors: For this Research Area, �therapeutic� activity means curing disease by eliminating or substantially reducing infective pathogens by administering antimicrobial pharmaceutical agents, with or without a host-directed therapy. Additionally, proposed therapeutic products should consider the impact on a healthy microbiome. Preventative treatments are not included in the scope of this Research Area. A therapeutic candidate refers to an advanced lead series, preclinical candidates, or a clinical candidate, that is a new chemical entity. This includes small molecules, natural products, nucleosides, or peptides of </= 40 amino acids, monoclonal antibodies, nanobodies, nanobody conjugate/fusion products, microbiome-based therapeutics or bacteriophages. Research Area 002 will support lead optimization, pre-clinical Investigational New Drug (IND) enabling studies, and Phase 1 clinical trials (or proof of concept Phase 2 clinical trials) of lead candidates with demonstrated therapeutic activities. This includes support for traditional, novel (e.g., small molecules) and non-traditional (e.g., including but not limited to phage, and host-directed) therapeutics for infectious diseases where patients lack effective interventions, as well as therapeutics that promote host-mediated resolution of disease. The scope of support differs depending on the developmental stage of the project being proposed, which is further discussed in the BAA Solicitation. Research Area 003 - In Vitro Diagnostics The objective of Research Area 003 is to develop innovative, technology platforms that will speed detection and identification of infectious viruses covering a broad panel of virus families, including viruses causing acute infections as well as those causing chronic infections. Technology platform innovation to achieve faster actionable sequencing results (approaching 2 hr) direct from primary clinical specimens, as well as more accessible workflow and configuration (i.e., point-of-care) are preferred. Furthermore, full sample-to-answer platform solutions are preferred. The system should accept specimen volumes from 0.5 to 5 milliliters (mL). The system should include nearly full automation (little or no hands-on activity after specimen has been loaded into system). Sample preparation components of the system should yield sufficient analyte recovery from a starting titer of 10-100 genomic copies per mL of biofluid for downstream analysis, including detection, identification, and characterization of the nucleic acid material. Innovations during platform development might include, for example: Automated sample prep for high recovery from low pathogen load. Faster specimen-to-answer for total test time <2 hours. Broad viral pathogen detection capability, covering one or more members of the priority pathogen families (see below). title: 2027 NIAID DMID Omnibus Broad Agency Announcement: Development of Medical Interventions for Infectious Diseases
description: INTRODUCTION: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), one of 27 institutes of the NIH, an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS); conducts and supports research to understand, treat, and ultimately prevent the myriad infectious, immunologic, and allergic diseases that threaten the health and longevity of human lives.Through a variety of research grants and contracts, NIAID�s Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) specifically supports extramural research to develop new medical interventions against infectious disease threats to include drug-resistant pathogens. NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to help address goals articulated in a number of strategic plans, such as in the Public Health Emergency Medical Countermeasures Enterprise Strategy and Implementation Plan (https://aspr.hhs.gov/PHEMCE/2024-PHEMCE-SIP/Pages/default.aspx), as well as current prioritized antimicrobial resistant threats identified by national death and infection estimates as determined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention�s (CDC) to prevent and control antimicrobial resistance (https://www.cdc.gov/antimicrobial-resistance/data-research/threats/index.html). In addition, NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to encourage projects that align with the NIH priorities of enhancing rigor & reproducibility, improving biosafety and biosecurity, and the use of complementary non-animal testing methods where appropriate. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is soliciting proposals to advance the research and development of promising candidate therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics for infectious diseases in each of three (3) Research Areas described below and more thoroughly discussed in the attached BAA Solicitation. An offeror should carefully review the content of the BAA Solicitation No. HHS-NIH-NIAID-BAA2026-1 for the comprehensive information regarding all requirements, the technical objective of each Research Area of this BAA Solicitation, instructions regarding the proposal submission, and a description of the evaluation and award process. Please note, due to the competitive nature of the BAA Solicitation, the NIAID is unable to offer advice or feedback regarding an offeror�s specific technical approach. Offerors should exercise their professional judgment when compiling their proposals in line with the requirements and specifications of the BAA Solicitation. Research Area 001 - Vaccine Candidates: The objective is to develop vaccine candidates through an early phase clinical trial that use a needle free (i.e., alternative to classical needle and syringe, see below for description) route of delivery to protect against infections caused by viral pathogens that include but are not limited to respiratory and vector borne viruses. The scope of this vaccine research area includes the preclinical development of a needle free vaccine candidate, IND enabling studies, limited process development, Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliant manufacturing, regulatory submissions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and conduct of a Phase 1 or early Phase 2 clinical trial. The scope of work must include a clinical trial. Offerors must propose a single vaccine candidate for protection against a specific viral pathogen. The vaccine candidate may provide a breadth of protection against other viral strains or viruses. A strong justification is required to support (1) the proposed vaccine antigen and platform for the disease indication, (2) the use of a clinically relevant adjuvant (if needed), and (3) a clinically relevant needle free route of delivery. Research Area 002 - Therapeutic Candidates: The objective is to develop safe, effective, new therapeutic products that will improve patient outcomes against serious infectious diseases for which there are no approved therapeutics, or for those that are refractory to treatment despite appropriate antimicrobial therapy or due to pathogen resistance. Infectious diseases caused by the following viruses, bacteria and fungi pathogens are targeted: Viral hemorrhagic fever viruses (e.g., EBOV, SUDV, MARV, LASV, hantavirus) https://www.cdc.gov/viral-hemorrhagic-fevers/about/index.html Encephalitic paramyxoviruses (e.g. hendra virus, nipah virus) Picornaviruses (broad spectrum approaches that include EV68, EV70 and coxsackie virus) At least two of the following (i.e., addressed with a broad spectrum antimicrobial): susceptible and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), susceptible and multidrug resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and susceptible and Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter (CRAB), with potential to improve patient outcomes in the clinic; Candida auris, Cryptococcus spp., Aspergillus fumigatus, and/or Mucorales Adjunct medical interventions to support or enhance effectiveness of antimicrobial agents to address underlying pathology that is not resolved after clearance of pathogens, may be considered. Important notice to Offerors: For this Research Area, �therapeutic� activity means curing disease by eliminating or substantially reducing infective pathogens by administering antimicrobial pharmaceutical agents, with or without a host-directed therapy. Additionally, proposed therapeutic products should consider the impact on a healthy microbiome. Preventative treatments are not included in the scope of this Research Area. A therapeutic candidate refers to an advanced lead series, preclinical candidates, or a clinical candidate, that is a new chemical entity. This includes small molecules, natural products, nucleosides, or peptides of </= 40 amino acids, monoclonal antibodies, nanobodies, nanobody conjugate/fusion products, microbiome-based therapeutics or bacteriophages. Research Area 002 will support lead optimization, pre-clinical Investigational New Drug (IND) enabling studies, and Phase 1 clinical trials (or proof of concept Phase 2 clinical trials) of lead candidates with demonstrated therapeutic activities. This includes support for traditional, novel (e.g., small molecules) and non-traditional (e.g., including but not limited to phage, and host-directed) therapeutics for infectious diseases where patients lack effective interventions, as well as therapeutics that promote host-mediated resolution of disease. The scope of support differs depending on the developmental stage of the project being proposed, which is further discussed in the BAA Solicitation. Research Area 003 - In Vitro Diagnostics The objective of Research Area 003 is to develop innovative, technology platforms that will speed detection and identification of infectious viruses covering a broad panel of virus families, including viruses causing acute infections as well as those causing chronic infections. Technology platform innovation to achieve faster actionable sequencing results (approaching 2 hr) direct from primary clinical specimens, as well as more accessible workflow and configuration (i.e., point-of-care) are preferred. Furthermore, full sample-to-answer platform solutions are preferred. The system should accept specimen volumes from 0.5 to 5 milliliters (mL). The system should include nearly full automation (little or no hands-on activity after specimen has been loaded into system). Sample preparation components of the system should yield sufficient analyte recovery from a starting titer of 10-100 genomic copies per mL of biofluid for downstream analysis, including detection, identification, and characterization of the nucleic acid material. Innovations during platform development might include, for example: Automated sample prep for high recovery from low pathogen load. Faster specimen-to-answer for total test time <2 hours. Broad viral pathogen detection capability, covering one or more members of the priority pathogen families (see below). title: Preventive Maintenance and Repair Services - Kahuku Training Area (KTA)
description: The Regional Contracting Office Hawaii (RCO-HI) has a requirement for preventive maintenance, inspection, testing, unscheduled assessment/trouble-call, and repair services for HVAC; fire alarm and mass notification; emergency lighting and exit signs; and lightning protection systems at Kahuku Training Area, Oahu, Hawaii. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, transportation, supervision, and other resources necessary to perform the requirement in accordance with the solicitation and Performance Work Statement. This solicitation is issued as Request for Quotations (RFQ) No. W912CN27QA008 and is a 100 percent Total Small Business Set-Aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 561210. The Government contemplates award of one firm-fixed-price requirements contract consisting of a base period and four 12-month option periods, with evaluation of the six-month option to extend services under FAR 52.217-8. The solicitation is conducted under the provisions of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. To be eligible for award, quoters must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), including current and complete representations and certifications, at the time of quote submission and at the time of award. Quoters are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments and other solicitation information through the closing date. Refer to Section L, pages 113�116, for quote-submission instructions and required submission content, and Section M, pages 120�121, for evaluation criteria. Quoters must submit all required documents, including the signed SF 1449 and acknowledgement of all amendments, completed pricing documents for all applicable priced CLINs, and the technical capability submission. Do not price Repair Services CLIN 0006 or its option-year counterparts; repair services will be ordered and priced after award through Contracting Officer-issued firm-fixed-price task orders. Written questions are due no later than 10:00 a.m. Hawaii Standard Time (HST), Thursday, 19 November 2026. Questions shall be submitted to both: Travis Tonini, Contract Specialist: travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil Keely K. Pool, Contracting Officer: keely.k.pool.civ@army.mil Completed quotations and all supporting documentation must be submitted electronically by email to Travis Tonini at travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil no later than 10:00 a.m. HST, Tuesday, 8 December 2026. Faxed quotations will not be accepted. A site visit at Kahuku Training Area is scheduled for Tuesday, 17 November 2026. Attendance is strongly encouraged but not mandatory. Offerors intending to attend must submit required visit-request information no later than 12:00 p.m. HST, Tuesday, 10 November 2026, to Travis Tonini for further instructions. (Solit file states 10:00 AM, but 12:00 p.m. is the official cut off).

title: ERDC Watercraft and Ship Simulator Support Services Multiple Award Task Order Contract
description: This is an unrestricted, full and open, Request for Proposal for the establishment of a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC).The ordering period will consist of a 24-month base period and three 12-month option periods, for a total potential ordering period of 60 months, if all options are exercised. The overall objective of this procurement is to augment ERDCs ship simulation capabilities by acquiring specialized, independent maritime simulation and engineering support services to deliver technically rigorous, time-sensitive simulation solutions to USACE navigation challenges. The Contractor shall independently execute designated simulation tasks, conduct technical analyses, and deliver finalized engineering reports as specified in individual Task Orders, leveraging external maritime expertise to support the USACE navigation mission. Navigation study services not directly connected with project maintenance and operations are considered commercial activities and not inherently governmental. (33 U.S.C. 2321(b)).

description: The Government requests that Responsive Strategic Sourcing for Services RS3 contractors review the attached Draft Performance Work Statements PWS for RS3-27-0014 Rapid Adaptation Prototyping and Threat Reaction RAPTR for the Signals Intelligence SIGINT and Quick Reaction Capabilities Sand QRC Division, Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance C5ISR Centers Engineering and Systems Integration Directorate ESID. RAPTR focuses on high-velocity Rand D, software-defined payloads, RF signal analysis, Super Intelligence Machine Learning SI ML for autonomous C5ISR systems, and rapid prototyping. Sand QRC Division is responsible for the research, development, engineering, and analytical modernization of critical warfighter technologies. To maintain technological overmatch, the Division expedites the delivery of near mid far term Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance C5ISR capabilities to meet rapidly evolving operational requirements. Sand QRC conducts advanced research and development across highly specialized domains including cyber operations, SIGINT, radar systems, and comprehensive intelligence analysis, exploitation, and dissemination. Utilizing an agile, iterative development pipeline grounded in soldier-centered design, the Division rapidly transitions concepts into fieldable solutions supported by continuous threat analysis, Modeling and Simulation Mand S, experimental trials, and rapid prototyping to ensure delivered capabilities are intuitive, operationally viable, and immediately effective on the modern battlefield. Sand QRCs operational mission spans the Continental United States CONUS, Outside the Continental United States OCONUS, and designated Hazard Duty Combat Zone areas. To execute these global operations, all Sand QRC projects are directed by a Government Project Lead who serves as the lead project integrator and maintains sole responsibility for all programmatic and technical aspects of assigned projects, to include the selection and leadership of the Integrated Project Teams IPTs employed to execute the projects. These specialized IPTs are composed of government personnel and contractor partners providing deep engineering, production, and technical expertise to ensure mission success under demanding conditions. title: Y1DA--523-418 B2 MH Addition Construction
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC) is conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for the Building 2 Inpatient Mental Health Addition at the Department of Veterans Affairs Boston Healthcare System (VABHS) - Brockton VA Medical Center located in Brockton, MA. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This project shall construct a new addition and renovate Building 2, Wing-C, Levels Basement through Level 4 and Roof. The basement level is Administrative Space. The new addition will be a five-story structure of approximately 6,000 gross square feet; the renovations on 5 levels of existing Building 2 will be approximately 8,600 square feet. The renovations and addition will take place in the Secure Inpatient Mental Health (Levels 2&3) and Residential Rehabilitation Treatment Program spaces (Levels 1&4). Work includes general construction, alterations, and certain other items. Services include but not limited to furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, and materials necessary to accomplish work for the demolition and replacement as required by specifications and drawings PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (Final Specifications and Drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued either as a Request For Proposal (RFP) in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) part 15, considering Technical and Price Factors or as an Invitation for Bid (IFB) in accordance with FAR part 14, considering Price only. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. This project is planned for advertising in January 2027. The magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000.00 and $20,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 236220 (size standard $45.0 million) applies to this procurement. The duration of the project is currently estimated at 730 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all construction related services such as: providing labor, materials and equipment required to complete the project as per contract documents prepared by an independent Architect-Engineer firm. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide company name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 236220. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAPM Magnitude of Construction listed above. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: No more than three (3) contracts that your company has performed within the last seven (7) years that are of comparable size, complexity, and scope to this requirement. Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates. Provide specific examples that relate aspects of previous projects to the proposed project. Describe specific technical skills and key personnel your company possess to perform the requirements described under description of work. Describe your Self-Performed** effort (as either a Prime or Subcontractor). Describe Self-Performed work in terms of dollar value and description. **Self-Performed means work performed by the offeror themselves, NOT work performed by another company for them for any of the project examples provided. It is requested that interested contractors submit a response (electronic submission) of no more than eight (8) single sided pages, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum that addresses the above information. This response must be submitted as a single application-generated (not scanned) PDF document that is less than or equal to 4MB in size. Please note that hard copies will not be accepted. Please also include a cover page, which includes, at a minimum: the company s name, address, Unique Entity Identifier (if available), socio-economic status, point-of-contact name, phone number, and e-mail address. Responses must include the Sources Sought number and project title in the subject line of their e-mail response. Submissions (responses) shall be submitted via email to the primary and secondary points of contact listed below by December 8, 2026 at 4:00 PM ET. No phone calls will be accepted. The Capabilities Statement submitted in response to this Sources Sought shall not be considered to be a bid or proposal. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and is neither to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to the respondents. After completing its analyses, the Government will determine whether to limit competition among the small business categories listed above or proceed with full and open competition as other than small business. At this time no solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the solicitation. If a solicitation is released it will be synopsized in Contract Opportunities at https://sam.gov/. It is the potential offeror's responsibility to monitor this site for the release of any solicitation or synopsis. Contracting Office Address: Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA) Program Contracting Activity Center (OFA PCAC) 6100 Oak Tree Blvd. Suite 490 Independence, OH 44131 Primary Point of Contact: Jacquelyn Wise Contract Specialist jacquelyn.wise@va.gov

description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE: (this is a Presolicitation Notice only. All documents, including, but not limited to, Specifications, Drawings, and Wage Determination, will be posted to the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module once the Request for Proposal is posted. Proposals or any other documentation is not required for this Presolicitation Notice. Please refer to paragraph 7 for more information). Action Type: Presolicitation Notice (Request for Proposals) Project Title: AT Courtyard Construction & Site Utility Infrastructure Project Location: Bettis Laboratory, West Mifflin, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania Site Owner / Operating Contractor: Naval Nuclear Laboratory / Fluor Marine Propulsion, LLC (PO Box 79, West Mifflin, PA 15122-0079) Procuring / Contracting Activity: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District (Notice regarding facility jurisdiction: Work will be performed on-site at Bettis Laboratory, an operating Naval Nuclear Laboratory facility, not a USACE facility. USACE personnel and contract administration will be coordinated via an on-site field trailer located at the project site.) (1) Point of Contact All inquiries concerning this presolicitation notice, attached specifications, and the upcoming Request for Proposals (RFP) must be directed in writing to the Contracting Officer and contract administration team: Contracting Officer: Leanna C. Lesefka, Contracting Officer Activity: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District Mailing Address: 1000 Liberty Avenue, Suite 2200, Pittsburgh, PA 15222 Email: leanna.c.lesefka@usace.army.mil Telephone: (412) 395-7549 Contract Specialist: Mario Taormina, Contract Specialist Activity: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District Email: mario.taorimina@usace.army.mil Telephone: (412) 395-7256 (2) Set-Asides Small Business Set-Aside Status: This proposed contract action is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside (see RFO Part 19). Competition is restricted exclusively to eligible, qualified small business concerns. Proposals submitted by concerns that are not small business entities under the applicable NAICS code will not be evaluated for award. Local area set asides (see RFO Part 26) do not apply to this action. (3) Codes for Services or Supplies North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Size Standard: $45.0 Million in average annual receipts Product Service Code (PSC): Y1PZ � Construction of Other Non-Building Facilities (4) Description of Requirement (i) Clear and Concise Description of Services / Construction Scope The Contractor shall furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, materials, testing, quality control, licenses, and transportation necessary to complete the construction of the AT Courtyard and associated utility infrastructure at Bettis Laboratory in West Mifflin, Pennsylvania, in strict accordance with the 100% QC Technical Specifications and contract drawings (draft). The contract action will be a stand-alone, firm-fixed-price (FFP) construction contract. The acquisition will be conducted via a Request for Proposals (RFP) utilizing Past Performance Price Tradeoff (PPTO) source selection procedures (see RFO Part 15). Under the PPTO evaluation structure, proposals will be evaluated based on Past Performance and Total Evaluated Price, with the Government reserving the right to award to a higher-priced offeror if the past performance record justifies the price differential. Summary of Work & Contract Line Item Structure: In accordance with the contract specifications, the work is organized into six (6) single-job payment CLINs: CLIN 0001 � Site Preparation and Demolition: Selective demolition and off-site disposal of designated asphalt and concrete pavements, existing safety fencing, concrete barriers, and existing underground utilities (water, storm, and gas lines); clearing, grubbing, topsoil stripping/stockpiling, traffic mats, and comprehensive erosion and sediment control measures. CLIN 0002 � Concrete: Reinforced cast-in-place concrete footers, concrete banding, exterior concrete paving and sidewalks (4,000 psi compressive strength) with medium-to-fine textured broom finish, expansion and contraction joint sealants, subbase/aggregate prep, bollard footings (5,000 psi), brick veneer installation, and precast concrete seating caps. CLIN 0003 � Earthwork: Site excavation, rock excavation provisions, proof-rolling with a 10-ton roller (5 complete passes), trenching, bedding course placement, compaction to not less than 95% maximum dry density per ASTM D1557 under slabs/pavements, landscape grading, and dewatering operations to maintain dry excavations. CLIN 0004 � Bioretention Area and Site Furnishings: Construction of a complete bioretention drainage facility; supply and installation of factory-finished outdoor site furnishings including horizontal strap steel benches, 4-seat picnic tables, pergola tables, cast aluminum chairs, planters, double-pedestal aluminum graphic panel frames, and extruded aluminum louvered pergolas (). All manufactured site furnishings must strictly comply with Buy America standards. CLIN 0005 � Raised Seated Area and Landscaping: Construction of reinforced concrete masonry unit (CMU) retaining walls with face brick and precast concrete caps; decomposed granite surfacing with organic stabilizer around trees; engineered multi-layered soil profiles for deep planters and containers (granular drainage medium, separation fabric, intensive base medium, and intensive growing medium); planting of deciduous trees, shrubs, perennials, and ground covers with a mandatory 12-month establishment warranty. CLIN 0006 � Site Utilities: Installation and testing of complete site utility distribution systems: Sanitary Sewers: Gravity SDR-35 PVC pipe, ASTM C478 precast concrete manholes with watertight cast iron frames/covers, low-pressure air testing, and 60-day mandrel deflection testing. Potable Water Distribution: Butt-fused high-density polyethylene (PE4710, DR11) pressure piping installed by certified fusion technicians (ASTM F3190), resilient-seated gate valves, polyethylene encasement for ductile iron fittings, hydrostatic testing, and AWWA C651 disinfection. Storm Utility Drainage: Smooth-wall corrugated HDPE culverts and underdrains, ASTM C913 precast concrete inlets (AASHTO H20 traffic loading), and reinforced cast-in-place concrete trench drains with pentagon security bolt grates. Site Natural-Gas Distribution: Medium-density polyethylene pipe (ASTM D2513 SDR 11) with electro-fusion joints, PE ball valves, cast iron valve boxes, and nitrogen pneumatic pressure and leak testing witnessed by USACE. Electronic Utility Markers: Continuous detectable warning tape and Government-Furnished (GFE) Omni Marker electronic balls placed every 20 feet and at every change in direction. Key Operational & Contract Administration Parameters: Operating Hours & Contractor Work Hours: Bettis Laboratory operates between 6:00 AM and 6:00 PM. Contractor work hours are strictly restricted to 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday, unless approved in writing by the Contracting Officer. U.S. Citizenship Strict Requirement: Only persons possessing verified United States citizenship are permitted on-site access to Bettis Laboratory facilities (foreign nationals require an 8-week prior approval from Naval Reactors). All personnel and delivery drivers must present REAL ID Act-compliant photo identification. Prohibited & Contraband Articles: Firearms, weapons, and knives with blades exceeding 2.5 inches are strictly prohibited. In addition, personal electronic devices (cameras, smartphones, recording equipment, laptops) are strictly prohibited inside the perimeter security fence without prior security authorization. description: Η μελέτη αυτή αφορά την ΠΡΟΜΗΘΕΙΑ ΠΕΤΡΕΛΑΙΟΥ ΘΕΡΜΑΝΣΗΣ 2027-2028 για τις ανάγκες του Δήμου ΝΕΑΣ ΠΡΟΠΟΝΤΙΔΑΣ για διάστημα δύο ετών και θα χρηματοδοτηθεί από ιδίους πόρους Τα υπό προμήθεια καύσιμα θέρμανσης πρέπει να έχουν τις προδιαγραφές που ορίζει το Ανώτατο Χημικό Συμβούλιο του Γενικού Χημείου του Κράτους σύμφωνα με τα ΦΕΚ 410/11-4-2001 και 872/4-6-2007 και θα πρέπει να είναι σύμφωνες με αυτές των ελληνικών διυλιστηρίων και ποιότητας όμοιας με εκείνη που παράγουν τα διυλιστήρια στην χώρα μας. Σε καμιά περίπτωση δεν επιτρέπεται η ύπαρξη ακαθαρσιών, χρώματος ή άλλων ξένων στοιχείων. Ο Δήμος διατηρεί το δικαίωμα να αποστέλλει δείγματα από τα καύσιμα ώστε να ελέγχεται τόσο η ποιότητα όσο και το αν πληρούν τις απαιτούμενες προδιαγραφές στο Γενικό Χημείο του Κράτους. Τα παραπάνω στοιχεία θεωρούνται ουσιώδη και απαράβατα εκτός αν αναφέρεται ότι αποτελούν προτίμηση ή επιθυμία της υπηρεσίας. Τα προς προμήθεια είδη κατατάσσονται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων CPV: 09135100-5 (πετρέλαιο θέρμανσης), Η ενδεικτική δαπάνη της προμήθειας προϋπολογίζεται στο ποσό των 1.170.237,60 € (943.740,00 € πλέον ΦΠΑ) Η εκτέλεση της προμήθειας θα γίνει σύμφωνα με τον Ν.4412/2016(ΦΕΚ147/8-8-2016) και τον Ν.3852/2010(ΦΕΚ87/7-6-2010). Η διάρκεια της σύμβασης θα είναι για δύο έτη και μετά από σύμφωνη γνώμη και των δύο συμβαλλόμενων δύναται να παραταθεί έως δυο έτη το ανώτερο, προκειμένου να καλυφθούν τρέχουσες ανάγκες του Δήμου, χωρίς τροποποίηση της συμβατικής αξίας. Η σύμβαση δεν χωρίζεται σε τμήματα διότι αφορά σε ένα είδος με διαφορετικούς κωδικούς στον προϋπολογισμό του Δήμου. Επίσης οι ποσότητες είναι ενδεικτικές. Εφόσον υπάρξει μία σύμβαση, μπορούν να γίνουν επουσιώδεις τροποποιήσεις και αυξομειώσεις ποσοτήτων μέσα στην ίδια σύμβαση, οπότε να μπορέσουμε να αξιοποιήσουμε όλες τις ποσότητες και να εξυπηρετηθούν όλες οι ευαίσθητες δομές του Δήμου. Η σύμβαση θα ανατεθεί με το κριτήριο της πλέον συμφέρουσας από οικονομική άποψη προσφοράς, βάσει τιμής και συγκεκριμένα: Κριτήριο βάσει τιμής για τα καύσιμα (χαμηλότερη τιμή), θεωρείται το μεγαλύτερο ποσοστό έκπτωσης επί τοις εκατό (%), στη νόμιμα διαμορφούμενη μέση τιμή πώλησης εκάστου είδους, την ημέρα παράδοσης τους, του Παρατηρητηρίου Τιμών Υγρών Καυσίμων του Υπουργείου Ανάπτυξης και Ανταγωνιστικότητας για το νομό Χαλκιδικής.

title: GPS Ground Segment Monitor Station Service (MSS)
description: Section 1: General Information Pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c), this is a Sources Sought Notice/ Request for Information (RFI) only. This notice is issued solely for conducting market research and planning purposes in accordance with RFO Part 10 and RFO Part 5. This announcement is for Market Research only and does not constitute a commitment, promise, or obligation by the Government to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or solicitation of any kind. The Government will not award a contract based on responses to this notice. The Space Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive (SFPAE) for Satellite Communications and Positioning, Navigation and Timing (SATCOM and PNT) is not seeking proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government will not pay for any information, bid preparation costs, or administrative expenses incurred in responding to this notice. Acquisition Attribute Program Baseline Details Notice ID / Solicitation Number SSC-GCS-MSS-SSN-2026 Sponsoring Agency / Office United States Space Force (USSF) / Space Systems Command (SSC) / MD31 Product Service Code (PSC) 1677 (Space Vehicle Remote Control Systems) North American Industry Classification (NAICS) 541715 (Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)) Classification & Security Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) / SECRET Facility Clearance Required Response Date & Time 8 December 2026 at 3:00 PM MST Primary Points of Contact Mr. Daniel Hilger, Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) Mr. Carl Griffin, Civil Navigation (CNAV) Project Lead Section 2: System Background & Scope of Work 2.1 Background The USSF is actively modernizing the GPS Ground Control Segment (GCS) to deliver enhanced Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) resilience and operationalize modernized civil and military signals. As part of this effort, USSF seeks to address necessary sustainment and modernization of its global PNT ground receiver network. The legacy ground control segment, the Architecture Evolution Plan (AEP), receives real-time tracking data from a total of 17 global monitor stations, 11 of which are estimated to face obsolescence in late 2028. USSF seeks options to transition to a modernized, sustainable ground segment architecture to maintain AEP's clock and orbit estimation engine (the Kalman Filter). To that end, the Government is requesting interested respondents submit statements of capability (SOCs) describing potential solutions to provide the capabilities described herein. Furthermore, the Space Force requires that any replacement ground receiver infrastructure not merely duplicate legacy capabilities but simultaneously address broader enterprise needs. The replacement architecture must serve as the primary operational enabler for: Civil Navigation (CNAV) Modernization: Providing independent, continuous signal-in-space tracking, integrity monitoring, and safety-of-life assurance for advanced civilian signals (L2C, L5, L1C) to support joint Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and international civil aviation commitments. Military Navigation (MNAV) & M-Code Operations: Integrating secure, high-fidelity tracking of military M-Code signals to enable robust anti-jam, anti-spoof Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR) operations and Regional Military Protection (RMP). 2.2 Spectrum & Signal Tracking Requirements To demonstrate that the required monitoring capability extends beyond legacy single-frequency L-Band observables, the proposed Monitor Station Service (MSS) must provide simultaneous multi-frequency, multi-code tracking across a growing constellation (up to 63 Space Vehicles). The solution must provide continuous tracking, measurement extraction, and observable processing across the following specific signal tiers: Signal Tier Frequency / Signal Type Capabilities & Processing Requirements Legacy Signals (Baseline Parity) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1P-codeless L1 C/A, L1P(Y) L2 (1227.60 MHz): L2P(Y) L2P-codless Continuous tracking, legacy LNAV message demodulation, pseudorange/carrier-phase measurement extraction, and legacy telemetry processing for core AEP Kalman Filter orbit/clock estimation continuity. Modernized Civil Signals (CNAV) L5 (1176.45 MHz): Safety-of-Life (SoL), L5I,L5Q L2 (1227.46 MHz): L2C (L2CM,L2CL) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1C (L1CD,L1CP) CNAV message demodulation, multi-frequency ionospheric delay cancellation, advanced signal quality monitoring (SQM), interference/jamming detection, and civil aviation safety-of-life (SoL) processing standards to support L5 Initial Operational Capability (IOC). Military Signals (Modernized) L1 / L2 M-Code (1575.42 MHz / 1227.46 MHz): Earth Coverage & Regional Military Protection (RMP) Direct M-Code acquisition and tracking, cryptographic channel decoding via NSA-certified security architecture, advanced anti-jam / anti-spoof protections, and Modernized User Equipment (MGUE) warfighter operational support. 2.3 Core Capabilities & Scope of Work The scope of this market research centers on identifying industry capabilities and realistic timelines to deliver an integrated, secure, and safety-certified Monitor Station Service (MSS) that interfaces seamlessly with AEP and external mission partners (FAA, NGA). The Government intends to acquire and take delivery of the software baseline and associated technical data rights to ensure long-term organic C2 baseline control and sustainment within the Government boundary. The Government is seeking responses that demonstrate capability across the following core technical tasks: Integrated Multi-Signal Ingestion: Acquire, process, format, and distribute raw binary and smoothed pseudorange, carrier phase, Accumulated Delta Range (ADR), and Signal Quality Metrics (SQM) across all legacy, CNAV, and MNAV signals listed in Section 2.2. Modular API & Service-Oriented Integration: Expose receiver monitoring and control capabilities through a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) utilizing standardized Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and messaging layers to decouple data feeds from underlying receiver hardware. Safety-of-Life Signal Assurance: Support rigorous software design assurance standards (certifiable up to Design Assurance Level D / DAL D per RTCA DO-278A / DO-178C) to provide real-time signal deformation detection, Code Carrier Coherence (CCC), and anomalous event alerting. Cryptographic & Boundary Security: Provide NSA-approved cryptographic handling capabilities for military key management, secure unclassified/classified cross-domain boundary routing, and continuous Risk Management Framework (RMF) security control validation in a secure government cloud/on-prem environment (IL5/IL6) to maintain an active DoD Authority to Operate (ATO). Receiver Security Certification (FSET): Provide receiver hardware, software, and firmware capable of achieving or maintaining security certification through the Space Systems Command (SSC) Functional Security Engineering Team (FSET) for deployment across global, unclassified, and collateral Secret monitoring locations, including supporting delta FSET recertification processes for component and cryptographic updates. Section 3: Information Requested from Industry To assist the government in conducting its statutory market research, all respondents are requested to organize their capability statements into the following structured sections: Part A: Corporate Profile Administrative Details: Company Name, Mailing Address, CAGE code, and Unique Entity ID (UEI). Socioeconomic Status: State your business size and any applicable socioeconomic designations under NAICS 541715 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.). Effort Description: TIGAR Exploratory Topic will forge entirely new paths to stabilizing regenerative tissues and organs by seeding the development of enabling technologies that can unlock temperature-flexible storage in increasingly larger and more complex biological systems. Solutions may involve any combination of new materials, artificial intelligence/machine learning, high-throughput screening methods, biological interventions, devices, processing methods, analytical technology, and packaging approaches that can overcome current roadblocks and yield a leap in the ability to store and distribute complex biologics, without introducing high cost or complexity. Strategies that reduce reliance on strictly controlled temperature zones and can ensure safe storage in a range of environmental conditions are preferred. While long-term temperature-flexible storage is ideal, any advance that removes logistical hurdles or establishes shelf-life stability at easy to maintain temperatures (preferably non-cryogenic) will be considered. Innovations at the cellular level without a strategy for deployment in thick tissues will not be considered. Please ensure to follow this opportunity for any updates. For more information on the TIGAR Exploratory Topic visit: https://arpa-h.gov/explore-funding/initiatives-and-sprints/tigar For information on Proposer's Day details and registration information, please see Special Notice ARPA-H-SN-26-142
